title: Storage Security and Encryption
description: Secure Azure storage with encryption at rest, Microsoft Defender for Storage, and network access controls.

data.text: Azure Storage security covers three layers: **identity and access** (who can do what), **network protection** (where requests can come from), and **encryption** (how data is protected at rest and in transit). Microsoft handles most encryption automatically, but you configure access policies and network rules.

All data in Azure Storage is encrypted automatically using **Storage Service Encryption (SSE)** with 256-bit AES keys. Microsoft manages the keys by default, but you can use **customer-managed keys (CMK)** stored in Azure Key Vault if your compliance policies require it.

data.title: Enable Customer-Managed Keys with Azure CLI
data.content: Configure a storage account to use a Key Vault key for encryption
data.code:
az storage account update \
  --name stdemostorage \
  --resource-group rg-demo \
  --encryption-key-source Microsoft.Keyvault \
  --encryption-key-name myKey \
  --encryption-key-vault https://myvault.vault.azure.net/

data.text: By default, storage accounts accept traffic from any network. You can restrict access to specific virtual networks or IP ranges using **firewall rules**, **service endpoints**, or **private endpoints**. These controls ensure that only authorized networks can reach your storage.

data.title: Enable Storage Firewall with Azure CLI
data.content: Allow access only from a specific virtual network
data.code:
az storage account network-rule add \
  --account-name stdemostorage \
  --resource-group rg-demo \
  --virtual-network /subscriptions/.../vnet/vnet-name

data.text: Microsoft Defender for Storage detects threats such as anomalous access patterns, data exfiltration attempts, and malware uploads. It integrates with Microsoft Defender for Cloud and generates security alerts you can act on.

terms.definition: Automatic encryption of all data at rest using AES-256 keys managed by Microsoft.
An encryption key stored in Azure Key Vault that you control, giving you the ability to rotate or revoke it.
A network interface that connects privately to a storage account over a virtual network.

data.title: Defense in Depth
data.text: Combine identity, network, and encryption controls. Even if a key leaks, network restrictions and monitoring give you time to detect and respond.

data.title: Exercise: Harden a Storage Account
data.description: Apply encryption, firewall, and Defender settings to a storage account.
steps: Verify that encryption at rest is enabled (it is by default).
Enable the storage account firewall and deny all public access.
Enable Microsoft Defender for Storage in the Azure Portal.
Attempt to access the storage account from a network not allowed by the firewall and confirm it is blocked.
data.expectedOutcome: A hardened storage account that rejects unauthorized network traffic and encrypts all data.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Azure Storage encrypts all data at rest by default.
Customer-managed keys let you control encryption in Key Vault.
Firewalls and private endpoints restrict network access.
Microsoft Defender for Storage provides threat detection and alerts.
data.takeaway: Layered security protects storage accounts from unauthorized access, network threats, and data exposure.
